text: Investing in stocks can be a great way to build wealth over time, but it requires careful research and strategy.
Bonds are generally considered safer than stocks, providing fixed interest payments and returning principal at maturity.
Real estate investment trusts (REITs) allow individuals to invest in real estate without having to buy properties directly.
Mutual funds pool money from multiple investors to purchase a diversified portfolio of stocks or bonds.
Index funds are investment vehicles designed to replicate the performance of a specific index, such as the S&P 500.
A diversified portfolio typically includes a mix of asset classes like stocks, bonds, and cash to reduce overall risk.
ETFs, or Exchange-Traded Funds, combine the diversification of mutual funds with the flexibility of stock trading.
A conservative investor may prioritize capital preservation and income generation over high returns.
Rebalancing your portfolio annually ensures that asset allocations remain aligned with your financial goals.
High-yield bonds offer greater returns but come with increased credit risk, especially during economic downturns.
Dollar-cost averaging involves investing a fixed amount regularly, helping reduce the impact of market volatility.
Tax-loss harvesting is a strategy that uses investment losses to offset capital gains, minimizing tax liability.
Compound interest allows your investments to grow exponentially over time as earnings generate additional earnings.
Liquidity refers to how easily an asset can be converted into cash without significantly affecting its value.
